{{Short description|Binary operation combining the vertex and edge sets of two graphs}}

[[File:Equivalentie.svg|thumb|A [[cluster graph]], the disjoint union of [[complete graph]]s]]
In [[graph theory]], the '''disjoint union of graphs''' is an operation that combines two or more [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graphs]] to form a larger graph.
It is analogous to the [[disjoint union|disjoint union of sets]] and is constructed by making the vertex set of the result be the disjoint union of the vertex sets of the given graphs and by making the edge set of the result be the disjoint union of the edge sets of the given graphs. Any disjoint union of two or more nonempty graphs is necessarily [[connectivity (graph theory)|disconnected]].

==Notation==
The disjoint union is also called the '''graph sum''' and may be represented either by a [[plus sign]] or a circled plus sign: If <math>G</math> and <math>H</math> are two graphs, then <math>G+H</math> or <math>G\oplus H</math> denotes their disjoint union.<ref>{{citation|title=Handbook of Discrete and Combinatorial Mathematics|series=Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications|first=Kenneth H.|last=Rosen|publisher=CRC Press|year=1999|isbn=9780849301490|page=515|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yJIMx9nXB6kC&pg=PA515}}</ref>

==Related graph classes==
Certain special classes of graphs may be represented using disjoint union operations. In particular:
*The [[Forest (graph theory)|forests]] are the disjoint unions of [[Tree (graph theory)|trees]].<ref>{{citation|page=627|title=Discrete Mathematics: An Introduction to Concepts, Methods, and Applications|first=Jerrold W.|last=Grossman|publisher=Macmillan|year=1990|isbn=9780023483318}}</ref>
*The [[cluster graph]]s are the disjoint unions of [[complete graph]]s.<ref>[http://www.graphclasses.org/classes/gc_1237.html Cluster graphs], Information System on Graph Classes and their Inclusions, accessed 2016-06-26.</ref>
*The [[regular graph|2-regular graphs]] are the disjoint unions of [[cycle graph]]s.<ref>{{citation|title=A First Course in Graph Theory|series=Dover Books on Mathematics|first1=Gary|last1=Chartrand|first2=Ping|last2=Zhang|author2-link=Ping Zhang (graph theorist)|publisher=Courier Corporation|year=2013|isbn=9780486297309|page=201|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zA_CAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA}}</ref>
More generally, every graph is the disjoint union of [[connected graph]]s, its [[connected component (graph theory)|connected component]]s.

The [[cograph]]s are the graphs that can be constructed from single-vertex graphs by a combination of disjoint union and [[Complement graph|complement]] operations.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Corneil | first1=D. G. | author1-link = Derek Corneil | last2=Lerchs | first2=H. | last3=Stewart Burlingham | first3=L. | title=Complement reducible graphs | doi=10.1016/0166-218X(81)90013-5 | mr=0619603 | year=1981 | journal=[[Discrete Applied Mathematics]] | volume=3 | pages=163–174 | issue=3| doi-access= }}</ref>
